text: Boyd Crowder stood outside the church with a rocket launcher.
That was Boyd.
"Fire in the hole." Then he pulled the trigger.
The rocket hit, and the church blew open in fire and smoke.
Wood cracked.
Windows burst.
The night lit up like judgment had fallen from the sky.
Boyd lowered the launcher, and the fire behind him kept climbing.
The flames could be seen from far off.
People would talk.
That made him dangerous, and it made him easy to find.
When Raylan heard the words, he knew.
"Fire in the hole." That was not just a phrase to him.
Raylan did not need much more.
Raylan knew Boyd Crowder from before the badge.
Before the trouble got this big.
They had been young men in the same hard country, working under.
The earth where coal dust got into a man's clothes and lungs.
Boyd had made it personal by being Boyd.
Raylan did not rush.
He checked his weapon, put on his hat.
The next blast had to be stopped.
Raylan found Boyd where trouble usually found him.
Close to people.
He had heard Boyd's speeches before.
Boyd talked like he always did.
Smooth.
Clever.
Too pleased with his own words.
Raylan kept watching his hands.
That was how Raylan worked.
Not much movement.
Boyd moved anyway.
The draw came fast.
Boyd reached, and Raylan fired.
That was how fast trouble can end when the right man is ready.
Raylan kept his gun on Boyd because alive did not mean harmless.
Boyd was on the floor now, hurt and breathing, his big speech cut short.
The rocket was not here.
The fire was not here.
Raylan had finished it.
The sirens would come.
The reports would be written.
The law was still standing.
